A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoboTwin 2.0. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-generation experiments, simulation benchmarks, grasp-adaptation evaluations, and real-world manipulation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and real-world experiments and adds code-quality, observer-cost, and error-detection/localization results in Appendices F and G.

M1.justification: The code-generation/refinement loop, five domain-randomization axes, and embodiment-aware grasp adaptation are retained. The added API, optional-observer, and code-example descriptions document the existing framework without establishing an algorithmic change between PDF versions.

E1.justification: v2 adds a curated set of 130 execution sequences for evaluating outcome detection and failure localization. The robustness comparison expands from five to eight manipulation tasks, adding Open Laptop, Press Stapler, and Turn Switch. The overall 50-task suite, object categories, embodiments, and real-world tasks remain unchanged; publishing the full benchmark table does not itself expand coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the six code-generation configurations, RoboTwin 1.0 grasping baseline, five policy models, and three real-world training alternatives. Human-written code supplies reference material for the new similarity analysis and case study, rather than an additional evaluated generation system. CodeBERT, UniXcoder, and CodeBLEU are used as evaluation measures.

E3.justification: Appendix D changes ACT/DP/DP3 budgets from 6,000/600/3,000 steps to epochs. Section 4.4 changes the reported perturbation target from object/robot poses to camera poses, and the texture pool changes from 12,000 to 11,000. CRSR is removed and Token is redefined as generated policy-code length. Section 4.3 revises the control description to released pretrained VLA weights. New code-quality and observer-evaluation protocols are also introduced. These are substantial reported changes; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds structural/semantic code-quality comparisons and observer-cost analysis. Appendix G.4 adds outcome-detection and failure-localization tests, a diagnostic case study, and failure examples; G.5 compares generated and human-written code. The expanded robustness ablation supplies additional evidence about domain-randomized training. These additions substantially deepen investigation of the generation mechanism and its limitations.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports 10 candidate programs per configuration, each executed 10 times; v2 replaces the candidate count with 'multiple' while retaining ten executions per refinement iteration. This removes repeated-generation count information without establishing fewer actual runs. Neither version reports confidence intervals, seed-based uncertainty, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises vanilla Top5-ASR from 47.4% to 57.6% for R1.0 and from 62.1% to 68.0% for R2.0. Robustness and simulation benchmark scores change extensively, and Appendix K supplies all 50 task rows versus 13 in v1. New results include 43.1% observer accuracy, 30% localization accuracy among correctly identified failures, and 6,894 tokens per observation. Real-world and embodiment-success results are retained. Changed budgets and aggregation prevent interpreting benchmark differences as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The program-level and task-level success-rate equations in Appendix G are retained. Neither version develops theoretical propositions or proofs. Added empirical metrics and their descriptions introduce no new mathematical derivation or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The four main contributions and the claims about scalable generation, domain randomization, embodiment adaptation, and sim-to-real transfer remain. The revised abstract makes the ten-real-demonstration baseline explicit but retains the 367% and 228% relative-improvement claims supported by the same real-world results.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive observer limitations involving hallucinated success, missed orientation errors, and invisible grasp parameters. It qualifies DP3 performance through perfect point clouds and background segmentation, and introduces an argument against a Real-to-Sim explanation for weak VLA results. It also removes v1's worst-case-guarantee inference and its discussion of unsolved articulated/dynamic tasks. These materially change the interpretation and qualification of the evidence.

D1.justification: Technical documentation is substantially revised through changed training-budget units, explicit DP3 segmentation, observer invocation and token-accounting details, generated/human code listings, and additional usage instructions. The dataset access path changes. Conversely, v1's allocation of 100 clean and 400 randomized trajectories per task–embodiment pair is omitted. These alter reproducibility information without establishing corresponding implementation changes in every case.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly contrasts its dual-arm code generation with GenSim2 and RoboGen, expands the RoboCasa discussion, and adds references supporting code-similarity measures. The broader positioning around simulation datasets, robotic foundation models, and domain randomization remains intact.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the abstract, domain-randomization explanation, dataset description, and experimental discussion are rewritten or condensed. Resource sections are merged, flexible-embodiment support moves to Appendix E, and code-generation material is consolidated and expanded in Appendix G. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adds the code-quality table, full 50-task benchmark table, benchmark-setting visualization, and code listings. It relocates the all-task code-generation table and heterogeneous-embodiment figure to appendices, restructures the main benchmark table, and removes Table 1's CRSR column. Figure sizing, placement, and several captions also change substantially across the document.

improvement.justification: The full benchmark table and new observer-quality, failure, and cost analyses make important claims more inspectable than in v1. The gain is tempered by lost dataset/run-count details and new inconsistencies: Section 4.3 describes five tasks while tabulating eight, and Appendix G.4 interprets recall as failure detection although its confusion-matrix counts treat success as positive. Greater transparency provides a modest net improvement, but these reporting problems limit the strength of the added evidence.
